newsitem.title: INDIA: India rulers postpone oil price meeting to July 2.
newsitem.headline: India rulers postpone oil price meeting to July 2.

text.p: India's ruling United Front coalition has postponed a meeting on oil prices, earlier scheduled for Friday, to July 2, the Press Trust of India quoted the alliance's spokesman as saying on Monday.

The news agency quoted spokesman Jaipal Reddy, who is also information and broadcasting minister, as saying the meeting had been deferred due to "preoccupations of some leaders". It did not elaborate.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Saturday that the 15-party centre-left coalition would decide whether to raise the prices of domestic petroleum products at its next meeting.

At its last meeting on June 16, the United Front postponed a decision on whether to raise prices to plug the government's mounting debt to state oil companies, estimated at 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) at the end of March.
The Economic Times said on Monday that the government was considering imposing a "windfall tax" on oil companies as part of a package of measures to rein in the mounting cost of oil subsidies.
The business daily said the package being drafted by senior civil servants would gradually dismantle administered prices and phase in reductions in tariffs on crude oil imports.
The set of measures would aim to reconcile disparate interests within Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's coalition.
